title: Day Zero: Control Plane Commissioning & Observability Proofs
summary: Draft runbook for initial commissioning of a private control plane (VPC/on-prem). Focus areas: safe day-zero deploy, observability 'proofs' (signals to validate), Terraform module decisions, scaling/rotation guidance, KV-cache warmup, and a short upgrade rollback plan.
context: This is a working playbook to guide an operator through first-time provisioning and validation for a private control plane installation. It intentionally blends checklists, short command snippets, and tests that produce clear success/failure signals ("observability proofs"). The goal is to make day-zero predictable and provide concrete artifacts for handoff to SRE and customer operators.
scope:
- Initial control plane bootstrap (seed cluster, control-plane services, ingress)
- Minimal viable observability to prove correctness (logs, traces, metrics, synthetic traffic)
- Terraform module notes and opinions that affected decisions
- Scale-up and rotation guidance for first 30 days
- Upgrade and rollback plan for minor control-plane updates
prereqs:
- VPC network (subnets/tgw) created and owner confirmed
- KMS/HSM keys provisioned and operator has access
- Registry with required images reachable from target environment
- Bastion host / jumpbox credentials available
- Terraform state backend (S3/GCS/remote) with correct ACLs
quick-commands:
ssh jumpbox@bastion.example.com
terraform init -backend-config=path=state/controlplane.tfstate
terraform apply -var-file=env/prod.tfvars -target=module.cp_seed -auto-approve
kubectl --context=cp-admin get pods -n redwood-controlplane
day-zero checklist (high level):
1) Confirm network & DNS
   - Validate VPC routes, NAT & egress policies
   - Confirm DNS zones and that controlplane.* resolves to expected ELB IPs
2) Apply seed infra (TF module cp_seed)
   - Targeted terraform apply for bootstrap resources only
   - Wait for seed bootstrap job to complete (watch logs)
3) Provision control-plane services (k8s controllers, api gateway, operator)
   - Use the provided helm charts in charts/controlplane/
   - pin images to sha digests for day-zero
4) Observability proof suite
   - Metrics: controlplane_api_request_count > 0 within 5m
   - Logs: api-server logs contain "started" and no repeated 5xxs
   - Traces: short synthetic trace shows path through auth->router->scheduler
   - Alert smoke: trigger and auto-clear a synthetic error
5) KV cache warmup
   - Run warmup job to populate prefix cache for top-10 call patterns
   - Confirm cache hit ratio > 60% for warmup targets
6) Canary route test
   - Create a canary route pinned to the new control-plane model
   - Validate latency P50/P95 under synthetic load
observability proofs (concrete tests):
- proof:controlplane-k8s
  - kubectl get nodes -> all Ready
  - kubectl get pods -n redwood-controlplane -> no CrashLoopBackOff after 10m
- proof:api-smoke
  - curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_TOKEN}" https://controlplane.example.com/health
  - Expect 200 with JSON {"status":"ok","version":"<semver>"}
- proof:trace-path
  - run go/e2e-tool --target controlplane --trace
  - Assert span sequence contains [auth, route, scheduler, persistence]
- proof:telemetry-pipeline
  - Send synthetic metric (cp.synthetic.request=1)
  - Confirm metric ingestion and chart shows point within 60s
terraform module notes (opinions & snipp:
- Module layout used for this run: modules/{network,ksm,cp_seed,cp_services,monitoring}
- Interface decisions:
  - cp_seed exposes: seed_bootstrap_script (string), admin_cidr (list), kms_key_id (string)
  - cp_services expects image_map (map) to allow operator image pin overrides
- Example minimal usage (pseudo-tf):
  module "cp_seed" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//modules/cp_seed?ref=v0.7.1"
    admin_cidr = ["10.0.0.0/24"]
    seed_bootstrap_script = file("scripts/day0-bootstrap.sh")
    kms_key_id = var.kms_key
  }
- Locking & state:
  - Always 'terraform init -upgrade=false' for day-zero unless security patch demanded
  - State write-locks must be enforced; operations team will own state unlocks
- Common pitfalls:
  - Not pinning module refs -> drift during parallel teams
  - Using count on critical resources (e.g., load_balancer) causes drift on deletion
scaling & rotation guidance (first 30 da:
- Scale policy (initial):
  - Control plane ASA targets: 3 controller replicas, 2 api frontends, 1 scheduler node pool
  - Horizontal autoscaler: enabled for frontend at cpu>60% sustained 5m
- Rotation windows:
  - Preferred maintenance: Tue-Thu 02:00-05:00 local to customer
  - For rolling rotations: cordon -> drain (grace 120s) -> upgrade -> uncordon
- Safe scale-up steps:
  - Add node pool (tf apply module/node_pool count=+1)
  - Verify node readiness and kube-system pods reschedule
  - Re-run observability proofs and synthetic load at scaled size
- Safe rotation checklist:
  - Ensure backups: etcd snapshot (s3://redwood-cp-backups/<env>/ts)
  - Disable canary routing and pause automatic rollouts
  - Drain node, confirm no API 5xx, proceed one-at-a-time
upgrade plan (minor patch, e.g., 0.7.x -:
- Pre-upgrade
  - Tag component versions and create upgrade ticket (JIRA-CP-XXX)
  - Run full observability proof suite, capture baseline metrics
  - Create etcd snapshot and verify integrity (sha256)
- Upgrade sequence
  1) Push image to private registry, tag sha
  2) Update cp_services image_map and run tf plan
  3) Apply to non-critical controllers first (scheduler -> analytics -> api)
  4) Monitor traces and request_errors for 15 minutes after each component
- Rollback
  - If >=2 consecutive 5xx spikes or controlplane-api unavailable for >5m: rollback
  - Rollback by pinning previous image sha in cp_services and performing terraform apply with -target=module.cp_services
  - Restore etcd from snapshot if cluster state inconsistent (see restore checklist)
restore checklist (etcd):
- Preconditions: cluster quiesced, write traffic disabled
- Steps:
  - kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment/etcd-restore=1 --replicas=1
  - etcdctl snapshot restore /data/restore.db --name cp-restore --initial-cluster "cp-0=http://127.0.0.1:2380"
  - Reconfigure manifests with restored peer urls
  - Bring up components and validate with proof:controlplane-k8s

open questions & decisions needed:
- Should cp_seed include a one-time K8s bootstrap job vs external bootstrap script? (pros/cons noted inline)
- Acceptable cache warmup targets: top-5 vs top-20 patterns — default to top-10 for initial rollout
- Security review date: schedule with security team before any non-trivial upgrade

notes:
- This document intentionally leaves room for operator-specific scripts in scripts/day0-*.sh. The goal is to be prescriptive about checks and tolerant about implementation.
- Keep this file short and point to detailed run scripts in the repo; this is meant to be 'what to prove', not 'all how-to lines'.
